scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP for both films (16:9, dark navy background, flat cartoon style, no molecular structures): haploid n = GOLD, diploid 2n = TEAL, triploid 3n = CORAL. Meiosis is a round gate labelled '2n → n' (the meiosis gate): one TEAL 2n cell enters and four GOLD n cells leave; any fusion of nuclei is a round gate marked '+'; mitosis is a thin GREY looping 'copy' arrow that never changes a token's colour. Cells and nuclei are drawn as simple dots or rounded blocks with a small white label (n, 2n, 3n). Plants are simple flat cartoons. The life-cycle wheel is a big ring drawn clockwise; any diagram not computed from data carries a small corner label 'schematic'. Title card 'Two Bodies, One Wheel' fades in over a green moss cushion on a grey stone wall, the cushion gently swaying.

scenes.tts: This green moss cushion is haploid, like a human egg. So where is the diploid moss?
scenes.visual: Zoom into the moss cushion on the wall. One leafy shoot is magnified; a single cell inside it glows GOLD with the label 'n: one set'. A small cartoon human egg cell appears beside it, also GOLD, labelled 'human egg: n'. A white question mark appears over the cushion with the words 'where is 2n?'
scenes.narration: This green moss cushion is haploid, like a human egg. So where is the diploid moss?

scenes.tts: A haploid cell carries one set of chromosomes. We write that as n, and colour it gold. A diploid cell carries two sets, written two n, and coloured teal.
scenes.caption: A haploid cell carries one set of chromosomes. We write that as n, and colour it gold. A diploid cell carries two sets, written 2n, and coloured teal.
scenes.visual: Two dots side by side. Left dot fills GOLD with one short white bar inside, label 'haploid = n'. Right dot fills TEAL with two white bars, label 'diploid = 2n'. A legend strip slides in along the bottom of the screen: GOLD n, TEAL 2n, and a greyed-out CORAL 3n with 'later'. The legend stays for the whole film.
scenes.narration: A haploid cell carries one set of chromosomes. We write that as n, and colour it gold. A diploid cell carries two sets, written 2n, and coloured teal.

scenes.tts: In a normal life cycle, only two kinds of event change that count. Meiosis halves it. Every fusion of nuclei adds the sets together. Mitosis, which copies a cell, never changes the count.
scenes.visual: Three icons drop in one by one. A meiosis gate labelled '2n → n': one TEAL 2n cell enters and four GOLD n cells leave. A + gate: two GOLD dots enter and one TEAL dot leaves. A GREY copy arrow: a GOLD dot loops round and comes out as two GOLD dots, same colour. On-screen rule: 'meiosis halves, fusion adds, mitosis copies'.
scenes.narration: In a normal life cycle, only two kinds of event change that count. Meiosis halves it. Every fusion of nuclei adds the sets together. Mitosis, which copies a cell, never changes the count.

scenes.tts: Now draw a land plant's life as a wheel. A diploid body, the sporophyte, or spore plant, makes spores by meiosis. Each spore is a single cell.
scenes.visual: A large ring draws itself clockwise. At the top sits a TEAL box labelled 'sporophyte (spore plant)'. Moving clockwise, the ring passes through the meiosis gate; out come small GOLD dots labelled 'spores, single cells'. A small white token marked '2n' rides the ring to the gate and flips to GOLD 'n' as it passes.
scenes.narration: Now draw a land plant's life as a wheel. A diploid body, the sporophyte, or spore plant, makes spores by meiosis. Each spore is a single cell.

scenes.tts: A spore divides by mitosis into a second body, the gametophyte, or gamete plant. It is already haploid, so it makes eggs and sperm by mitosis.
scenes.visual: The token, now GOLD, rides on past two GREY copy arrows. A GOLD box labelled 'gametophyte (gamete plant)' grows from the spore at the bottom of the ring. From it bud a GOLD egg and GOLD sperm, with a GREY copy arrow beside them, labelled 'by mitosis'. The token stays GOLD the whole way.
scenes.narration: A spore divides by mitosis into a second body, the gametophyte, or gamete plant. It is already haploid, so it makes eggs and sperm by mitosis.

scenes.tts: Then sperm and egg fuse. The zygote, the single fertilized cell, has two sets again. It divides by mitosis into a new sporophyte.
scenes.visual: Egg and sperm slide into the + gate; out comes one TEAL dot labelled 'zygote: 2n'. The token flips to TEAL. GREY copy arrows carry it back up the ring, where the TEAL sporophyte box re-forms. The wheel is now closed.
scenes.narration: Then sperm and egg fuse. The zygote, the single fertilized cell, has two sets again. It divides by mitosis into a new sporophyte.

scenes.tts: So the wheel has two arcs. From meiosis to fertilization, the path is gold. From fertilization to the next meiosis, it is teal. Other fusions can make other labels, as the next film shows.
scenes.visual: The ring re-colours: the arc from the meiosis gate clockwise to the + gate fills GOLD; the arc from the + gate back to the meiosis gate fills TEAL. The + gate on this ring carries a small label 'fertilization'. The two gates pulse in white. The boxes on the ring fade to plain outlines so only the arcs and gates are bright.
scenes.narration: So the wheel has two arcs. From meiosis to fertilization, the path is gold. From fertilization to the next meiosis, it is teal. Other fusions can make other labels, as the next film shows.

scenes.tts: Now the moss. The gold arc swells into the leafy green shoot, so that shoot is the gametophyte. A sperm swims through a film of rain or dew to an egg on it.
scenes.visual: The GOLD arc balloons into a cartoon leafy moss shoot, labelled 'gametophyte, n'. Rain drops fall and a thin blue water film spreads over the shoot tips; a tiny GOLD sperm with a tail swims along it to a GOLD egg at a shoot tip.
scenes.narration: Now the moss. The gold arc swells into the leafy green shoot, so that shoot is the gametophyte. A sperm swims through a film of rain or dew to an egg on it.

scenes.tts: The teal arc shrinks to a thin stalk and a capsule. That is the diploid moss. Meiosis in the capsule makes the spores.
scenes.visual: The + gate fires at the shoot tip. The TEAL arc shrinks to a thin TEAL stalk topped by a TEAL capsule growing out of the leafy shoot, labelled 'sporophyte, 2n: the diploid moss'. The question mark from the opening snaps onto the capsule and turns into a tick. Tiny GOLD spores puff from the capsule through a meiosis gate.
scenes.narration: The teal arc shrinks to a thin stalk and a capsule. That is the diploid moss. Meiosis in the capsule makes the spores.

scenes.tts: Now a fern. Here the arcs swap sizes. The big frond is the sporophyte, teal. Spore cases under it make spores by meiosis.
scenes.visual: The moss slides off. A tall cartoon fern frond grows in, filled TEAL, labelled 'frond = sporophyte, 2n'. The ring behind it redraws with a fat TEAL arc and a thin GOLD arc. Small brown dots under the frond leaflets are labelled 'spore cases'; GOLD spores drift out of a meiosis gate.
scenes.narration: Now a fern. Here the arcs swap sizes. The big frond is the sporophyte, teal. Spore cases under it make spores by meiosis.

scenes.tts: Each spore grows into a small plant on the ground. Gold or teal: the spore, and that little plant?
scenes.visual: One spore lands on the soil and a tiny flat plant starts to grow from it, both drawn in plain white outline with no colour. Two large outlined boxes 'spore ?' and 'little plant ?' pulse. A GOLD swatch and a TEAL swatch hover side by side.
scenes.narration: Each spore grows into a small plant on the ground. Gold or teal: the spore, and that little plant?

scenes.visual: Hold the uncoloured spore and little plant. A thin timer bar shrinks across the bottom of the screen.

scenes.tts: Both gold. They come after the meiosis gate, and no fusion has happened yet. The little plant is a prothallus, a flat, often heart-shaped gametophyte. It lives on its own.
scenes.visual: The spore and the little plant fill GOLD together. The ring flashes, showing both sitting on the GOLD arc between the meiosis gate and the + gate. The little plant becomes a heart-shaped GOLD prothallus, labelled 'prothallus = gametophyte, n'. A blue water film appears and a GOLD sperm swims to an egg on it.
scenes.narration: Both gold. They come after the meiosis gate, and no fusion has happened yet. The little plant is a prothallus, a flat, often heart-shaped gametophyte. It lives on its own.

scenes.tts: Now compare your own wheel. In humans, meiosis makes eggs and sperm directly. The gold arc shrinks to the gametes alone. There is no haploid body.
scenes.visual: A third ring appears beside a simple human silhouette. Its TEAL arc is almost the whole circle; the GOLD arc is a tiny sliver containing just an egg and a sperm. Label 'human: no haploid body'. The fern ring stays small in the corner for comparison.
scenes.narration: Now compare your own wheel. In humans, meiosis makes eggs and sperm directly. The gold arc shrinks to the gametes alone. There is no haploid body.

scenes.tts: In the green algae closest to land plants, the teal arc shrinks instead. The zygote is often the only diploid cell. It undergoes meiosis when it germinates.
scenes.visual: A fourth ring beside a cartoon green alga cell. Now the GOLD arc is almost the whole circle; the TEAL arc is a single TEAL dot labelled 'zygote: the only 2n cell', which passes straight into the meiosis gate. The four rings (moss, fern, human, alga) line up in a row, each with very different arc sizes.
scenes.narration: In the green algae closest to land plants, the teal arc shrinks instead. The zygote is often the only diploid cell. It undergoes meiosis when it germinates.

scenes.tts: So size tells you nothing. The big body can be gold or teal. Find meiosis and fusion first, and every label follows.
scenes.visual: The four rings shrink and stack. In each, only the meiosis gate and the + gate glow white; the arcs between them colour themselves GOLD or TEAL automatically. On-screen: 'find meiosis and fusion; the labels follow'.
scenes.narration: So size tells you nothing. The big body can be gold or teal. Find meiosis and fusion first, and every label follows.

scenes.tts: One problem remains. In both the moss and the fern, sperm swim to the egg through water. What can a plant do where there is none?
scenes.visual: The moss and fern water films glow blue. Pan up to a cartoon pine tree on a dry ridge under a hot sun; no water film anywhere. A white question mark hangs over a pine cone.
scenes.narration: One problem remains. In both the moss and the fern, sperm swim to the egg through water. What can a plant do where there is none?

scenes.visual: End card: the hexagon mascot holds a small wheel with a GOLD arc, a TEAL arc and two white gates. Line: 'Find meiosis and fusion; the labels follow, whichever body is big.'
